title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, "Analysis of homozygous transgenic lines" vs. Figure 3 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states "Comparative shoot-length, root-length and fresh wt. taken after 10 days-stress indicated 7PcINO1-line, 10PcIMT1-line and 6DC1-line as the best in terms of growth parameters (Fig. 3a–c)", while the caption of the same figure reads "Comparative phenotypic study for shoot-length, root-length and fresh-weight of transgenics with untransformed lines under variable NaCl stresses kept for 7 days". The duration of the stress treatment underlying Fig. 3 is therefore reported as both 7 and 10 days.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, "Construction of expression vectors ... generation of salt-tolerant transgenic rice lines" (Southern/segregation paragraph)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same paragraph first states that "Homozygous T₂ lines ... were selected for Southern blot analysis of plants from PcINO1-lines (110 plants), PcIMT1-lines (153 plants) and ... DC1 (98 plants) lines", but then refers to the outcome of that analysis as "Southern positive T₃ PcINO1-plants exhibiting additional single-copy integration". The generation on which the Southern analysis was performed (T₂ vs T₃) is internally contradictory.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, segregation analysis sentence ("Southern positive T₃ PcINO1-plants ... were used for segregation analysis (Supplementary Tables S4a–S6a)")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Segregation analysis is applied to plants described as derived from already-selected homozygous (T₂) lines. Homozygous single-locus transgenic lines by definition do not segregate (100% transgene transmission), so performing/reporting a Mendelian segregation analysis on them is methodologically incoherent; segregation data must come from hemizygous (T₁) progeny.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, first section — repeated citation of Supplementary Fig. S5g–m
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The identical supplementary panel set is cited for two different experiments: "Among the T₀ putative transgenics (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m) hptII gene specific PCR positive plants were selected" and "Homozygous T₂ lines showing the presence of hptII gene at 1 kb, PcINO1 gene at 1.5 kb and PcIMT1 gene at 1.1 kb region respectively (Supplementary Fig. S5g–m)". One of the two citations must be wrong, as a single set of gels cannot document both T₀ screening and T₂ homozygous-line genotyping.

The Abstract asserts that "The PcIMT1-lines or the double transgenic lines (DC1) ... were less efficient in such respect", yet the Results report that "Even after 300 mM salt stress for 10 days, 7PcINO1-line, 10PcIMT1-line and 6DC1-line fully recovered their normal physiological activity" and that "Chlorophyll estimation after 15 days of salt withdrawal prominently indicated recovery of chlorophyll content in all transgenic lines". The reported phenotypic/physiological evidence does not support the stated superiority of PcINO1 lines over PcIMT1/DC1 lines.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, "Test of allergenicity for candidate protein(s)"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated alignment lengths and protein sizes are inconsistent with the quoted match percentages: 110 residues matched against a 346-aa allergen is 31.8%, and 137 residues against a 367-aa allergen is 37.3%, whereas the text reports "a match of only 25.5% ... and 24.8%". No window/identity basis is given to reconcile these figures, and the 37% value would exceed the conventional FAO/WHO 35% cross-reactivity threshold used to infer potential allergenicity, undermining the conclusion drawn.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 5a,b description of INO1 transcript fold-changes
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: "7PcINO1-line recorded a ~2.61 fold increase in the INO1 transcript under stress as against ~0.5 fold in 10PcIMT1 line and 0.67 fold in 6DC1 line" — values of 0.5 and 0.67 represent reductions relative to the reference, not 'increases'; describing them as increases misreports the direction of change (and the ~2.61 figure is reported with a precision unjustified for semi-quantitative gel densitometry).
